```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(performance)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(123)
n <- 200

# ============================================
# THREE DIFFERENT HETEROSCEDASTICITY PATTERNS
# ============================================

# Example 1: GOOD - Constant variance
# Standardized measurements with consistent error - truly random around mean
x_good <- runif(n, 5, 30)
y_good <- 0.5 + 0.8 * x_good + rnorm(n, 0, sd = 0.5) # Constant SD, no trend
m_good <- lm(y_good ~ x_good)

# Example 2: MILD - Linear increase in variance
# Like allometric growth where larger organisms show more variability
x_mild <- runif(n, 5, 30)
y_mild <- 0.5 + 0.8 * x_mild + rnorm(n, 0, sd = 0.2 + 0.02 * x_mild)
# SD increases from 0.2 to 0.8 (subtle increase)
m_mild_hetero <- lm(y_mild ~ x_mild)

# Example 3: SEVERE - Poisson-like pattern (mean = variance)
# Count data: parasite abundance, egg counts, etc.
# Variance increases nonlinearly with mean
x_severe <- runif(n, 5, 30)
mean_count <- 1 + 0.6 * x_severe
y_severe <- rpois(n, lambda = pmax(mean_count, 0.1))
m_severe_hetero <- lm(y_severe ~ x_severe)

# Generate plots
p_het1 <- plot(check_model(m_good, check = "homogeneity"))
p_het2 <- plot(check_model(m_mild_hetero, check = "homogeneity"))
p_het3 <- plot(check_model(m_severe_hetero, check = "homogeneity"))

# Show all three
p_het1 + p_het2 + p_het3

```

## Raw data comparison

```{r}
# Visualize the raw data to understand the patterns

data_all <- tibble(
  scenario = c(
    rep("Good: Constant variance", n),
    rep("Mild: Linear increase", n),
    rep("Severe: Count data (Poisson)", n)
  ),
  x = c(x_good, x_mild, x_severe),
  y = c(y_good, y_mild, y_severe)
)

data_all %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Body size (cm)", y = "Measurement") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

```
